intro: Hi class — I'm Dr. Marcus Vela. I help design wind turbines, and the thing I love most is that a turbine is honest: it records everything it does, minute by minute. Today we'll watch one real turbine work for half a day. Then I want every group to tell me what you noticed about the shape it drew. There are no wrong answers — just different angles.
act1Post: Every dot you just saw is one real minute of one turbine's life — the wind speed it felt, and the power it made. Two numbers each. Put them all on the same plane and the turbine draws a curve. Don't name the shape yet. Tell me what you see — every group.
act2Picker: Now you investigate. Different tools test different ideas. Fitting a curve asks 'what equation matches?' Differences ask 'is it really a parabola?' Splitting it into zones asks 'where does the model actually hold?' There's no right tool — pick what fits the wonderings up there, and write down what each one shows.
act3Top: No answer was wrong. Every group's notice and wonder was a real piece of the picture — even the ones that contradicted each other. Below, you'll see what every group found, side by side. Then I'll show you the math that ties it together.
act3Closing: Thanks for modeling with me. A parabola fits the rising part of this curve beautifully — but the real physics is a little wilder, and that flat top was a design choice, built in on purpose. The next time you drive past a wind farm, you'll know exactly what those blades are doing, and why every model has limits.
